title: Review of c18's cog no-fission negative: on fresh seed 5 from noise, unperturbed cogs stay single (1 persistent split in 1000 t), and with k0 h x0.75 new cogs come only from an expanding ring that becomes worms and breaks up, not from cog fission; Supported
summary: I looked at scr_k1m09.png and fscreen*.txt. The screen's planted-cog snapshot (scr_cog.npz) is not in the contribution (npz files are not imported), so I could not replay the 48 planted runs. Instead I ran the finding's world.py with labkit from full-domain noise on seed 5 (192^2, t=1000), unperturbed and with two of the screen's single-kernel perturbations. Unperturbed: 11 shelled cogs persist from t~200 at near-constant size (persistent area ratio 2.18), 1 persistent split in the whole run (rerun/base). k0 h x0.75: the cogs again stay single, but at t~395 one body grows into an expanding closed ring (as in the screen's k1 m x0.9 run and lcn) that breaks into worms and then into many cogs by collision (rerun/k0h075/sheet.png t=395-1000); labkit counts 2 persistent splits (generation 2) against 74 merges, and the new cogs come from worm fragments. k1 m x0.95 from noise never settles into cogs: a churning sea of 28-41 short-lived bodies (0 persistent tracks, merge/split 1.07). So on this seed no mature cog divides, and the only route to more cogs is an unbounded front breaking up, as the finding concludes.

observations.D: rerun/base/FACTS.md: 11 persistent cogs, 1 persistent split in t=1000; rerun/k0h075/sheet.png t=395-1000: expanding ring -> worms -> fragments, no cog fission; rerun/k1m095/FACTS.md: 0 persistent tracks

seeds_run.result: pass: no mature-cog fission unperturbed or with k0 h x0.75; k1 m x0.95 gives a churning sea from noise

controls_run.D: the unperturbed world on the same seed (rerun/base) beside two single-kernel perturbations

not_checked: the planted-cog screen itself (its starting snapshot is not shipped)
verdicts.limitation: My runs start from noise, not from the planted mature cog, so they test the finding's conclusion (no fissioning state near the cog) only for two perturbations, and k1 m x0.95 from noise is not comparable to the planted run. Shipping the planted state as a small text or PNG file would let reviewers replay the screen.
